newsitem.title: USA: Clinton and "clone" entertain news broadcasters.
newsitem.headline: Clinton and "clone" entertain news broadcasters.

text.p: With a TV impersonator playing his "clone," President Bill Clinton poked fun at himself and U.S. news broadcasters on Thursday night at a black-tie dinner that was much tamer than last year's edition.

Clinton, on crutches after knee surgery last month, opened a 10-minute monologue at the Radio-Television Correspondents' Association annual dinner by joking about former President George Bush's recent parachute jump.
"I want all of you to know that until recently, I had planned out a really dramatic entrance to this dinner -- and then George Bush stole my thunder!" he quipped.
Bush, who was forced to parachute from a crippled plane as a Navy aviator in World War II, skydived for fun with army parachute experts in Arizona two weeks ago.
"I mean, look at this," Clinton said. "This guy is 72 years old and he jumps out of a plane at 12,000 feet. He lands without a scratch. I fall six inches and I'm crippled up for six months!"
The 50-year-old president underwent surgery on March 14 after he tore a tendon in his right knee by stumbling on some steps at the Florida estate of Australian golfer Greg Norman.
Clinton lampooned television news coverage of his injury, saving one of his sharpest barbs for the sometimes overly dramatic style of reporting of the Cable News Network.
"Within an hour of the accident, CNN had composed ominious theme music and put up a graphic -- 'Breaking News, Breaking Knees," he said as 2,500 people in audience howled.
But the highlight of Clinton's lighthearted performance came when he introduced his "clone" -- comedian Darryl Hammond, who impersonates him on the NBC comedy show "Saturday Night Live."
Hammond, mimicking Clinton's Arkansas drawl, recited some of the president's favourite slogans as Clinton and his wife Hillary -- and their broadcast hosts -- roared with laughter.
"We must find common ground," the comedian intoned. "We're going to build a bridge to the 21st Century...Yadeeyadeeyada!"

The comic headliner at the dinner was Norm MacDonald, also a regular on Saturday Night Live. He caused gales of laughter when he referred impishly to broadcasters' now-infamous dinner in 1996, when radio personality Don Imus made insulting jokes about the president, Mrs. Clinton and many prominent broadcasters in attendence.

Imus's performance caused much soul-searching among those who heard it over whether it should have been condoned -- Mrs. Clinton privately told friends she was tempted to walk out -- -- and led the association to apologise to the president and his wife.
MacDonald's most mischievous moment came when he did an impersonation of former Sen. Bob Dole, Clinton's 1996 Republican rival for the presidency.
"Ladies and gentlemen of the press, the hell with all of you! You cost me the damn election. You can kiss my a--, every last one of you," he said, aping Dole's laconic speech pattern perfectly.
